title: Teaching Salah to Children and the Importance of Early Guidance

text_simplified: Parents must teach their children salah from the age of seven, and may discipline them gently if they do not adhere to it by the age of ten. Children should also be guided toward goodness and gradually accustomed to acts of worship. This text explains the importance of early religious tarbiyah (upbringing).

review_defects.arabic: ويمكن ضربهم بلطف إن لم يلتزموا بها في سن العاشرة
review_defects.english: and may discipline them gently if they do not adhere to it by the age of ten
review_defects.why: The Arabic explicitly says 'hit them gently' (ضربهم بلطف), which is a direct paraphrase of the hadith about commanding children to pray at seven and hitting them at ten. The English 'discipline them gently' softens and omits the specific action of hitting, altering the religious ruling.
Arabic 'الآباء' means fathers, not parents. The English broadens the obligation to include mothers, which may not be the intended meaning.
